clue.text: Dick, soldier and seer

parts.note: a private is a soldier of the lowest rank
a seer is one who sees, and the organ that sees is an eye

explanation.surface: A list of three figures: a detective, a soldier and a prophet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dick' is old slang for a detective, not a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Dick is slang for a detective, and a hired investigator is the same thing.

clue.text: Castle that's a new addition to our defences

definitions.text: a new addition to our defences

parts.note: the rook is also called the castle in chess
i.e. stands for 'that is'

explanation.surface: A castle described as the latest part of our fortifications.
explanation.definitionFit: A rookie is a raw recruit, newly joined to the forces.

clue.text: State legislator shows anger over Southern bloodsuckers

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the piece before sits above the next

parts.note: VA is Virginia, a US state
an MP is a Member of Parliament
ire is anger
S is southern

explanation.surface: A state politician gets angry at bloodsucking southerners.
explanation.definitionFit: Vampires are blood-drinking creatures of folklore, also bats that feed on blood.

clue.text: Gentle care brings ancillary vessel to Cape

parts.note: a tender is a small boat serving a larger ship
a ness is a headland or cape

explanation.surface: A small support boat brings tender care to a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenderness is kindly, careful affection.

clue.text: Good husbandry class for travellers

explanation.definitionFit: Good husbandry is thrifty management of resources; economy class is the cheapest seating for air travellers.

clue.text: Muslim ruler in eastern border rising

parts.note: E is eastern

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a rim is a border

explanation.surface: A Muslim ruler appears on the eastern border as it rises.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a prince or commander in Muslim lands.

clue.text: Tedder's great blow?

parts.note: a tedder is a machine that spreads hay to dry, so its work makes hay; a punch called after that is a mighty swing

explanation.definitionFit: A haymaker is a powerful swinging punch, and also one who makes hay, like a tedder.

clue.text: Zest of Ulster Protestant premier

parts.note: an Orangeman is a member of the Protestant Orange Order of Northern Ireland
Robert Peel was a British prime minister

explanation.surface: The enthusiasm of a Protestant prime minister from Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Zest is the outer rind of citrus fruit, used to flavour food.

clue.text: A million and nothing to show? Some yarn!

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for a million
the letter O looks like zero, nothing
Hair is a famous rock musical show

explanation.surface: Someone with a million and nothing to show for it is spinning a tall tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some yarn!' sounds like disbelief at a tall story, but it is literal: a kind of wool.
explanation.definitionFit: Mohair is a wool spun from Angora goat hair, a type of knitting yarn.

clue.text: Stop leader of new party by armed force

parts.note: a comma is a stop in punctuation

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here of new

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: Halting a new political party's leader by military means.
explanation.definitionFit: A commando is a soldier of a raiding unit, an armed force trained for assaults.

clue.text: Scandinavian has no right to reject titles

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to reject is to throw back, so the word for titles is turned around

parts.note: titles are names

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian who has no right to refuse honorific titles.
explanation.definitionFit: A Norseman was a Viking, a person of ancient Scandinavia.

clue.text: Almost uncanny means of river control

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: uncanny means weird

explanation.surface: A spooky way of managing a river's flow.
explanation.definitionFit: A weir is a low dam built across a river to regulate its flow.

clue.text: Sympathetic type on long desert trek?

definitions.text: Sympathetic type on long desert trek?

parts.words: Sympathetic type on long desert trek?
parts.note: a thirsty traveller crossing the desert would long for a source of water

explanation.definitionFit: A well-wisher is someone who hopes for another's good fortune, a kindly supporter.

clue.text: Sheep with a neck-feather? That's crazy!

parts.note: a male sheep is a ram, and 'with' makes it possessive: the ram's
a hackle is one of the long feathers on a bird's neck

explanation.surface: Picturing a sheep sporting a cockerel's neck feather and calling it mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crazy' here means rickety, as in crazy paving or a crazy old shed.
explanation.definitionFit: Crazy in the sense of tumbledown or rickety matches a building in a ruinous state.

clue.text: Unhappy peeress hid from garden nymphs

indicators.note: unhappy signals the letters are put into a disturbed order

explanation.surface: A miserable noblewoman hides from the fairies at the bottom of the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unhappy' rearranges PEERESS and HID; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hesperides were Greek nymphs who tended a garden of golden apples.

clue.text: Grassland she would have kept under control

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or grassland in poetry
she would contracts to she'd

explanation.surface: Grassland a woman would have kept tidy and in check.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep a dog under control is to hold it on a lead, so restrained.

clue.text: She provided "butter for The Royal slice of bread" (Milne)

definitions.text: She provided "butter for The Royal slice of bread" (Milne)

parts.words: She provided "butter for The Royal slice of bread" (Milne)
parts.note: in A. A. Milne's poem The King's Breakfast the dairymaid asks a cow of a Channel Island breed for the king's butter

explanation.definitionFit: An Alderney is a breed of dairy cattle from a Channel Island, the cow in Milne's poem.

clue.text: One goddess hides strange arts from another

indicators.note: the goddess's name hides the scrambled letters by enclosing them

parts.note: Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

indicators.note: strange signals the letters of arts are jumbled

explanation.surface: One goddess conceals odd arts from a rival deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges ARTS into STAR, which 'hides' puts inside ATE. 'another' is the definition: a further goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: Astarte was a Phoenician goddess of love and fertility, so another deity besides the first.

clue.text: He makes over Roman coin to Italian gentleman

indicators.note: to means the first piece is joined on to the second

parts.note: the as was a copper coin of ancient Rome
signor is the Italian for Mr, a gentleman

explanation.surface: A man transfers an ancient coin to an Italian gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: An assignor is a person who transfers property or rights to someone else.

clue.text: How, they say, eldest son got post

indicators.note: they say signals that the words are spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: the eldest son is the male heir, an heir male

explanation.surface: Asking how the firstborn son received his mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How' and 'got' are link words in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmail is mail carried by aircraft, letters sent by plane.

clue.text: Poor offering champagne? Times have changed

parts.note: the widow is slang for champagne, from Veuve Clicquot ('veuve' is French for widow)

indicators.note: have changed tells us the letters of Times are rearranged

explanation.surface: Complaining that champagne is a poor gift nowadays because times have changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have changed' turns TIMES into SMITE. The widow's mite is the Gospel story of a poor widow's tiny gift.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible a destitute widow gives two tiny coins, a small but sincere gift.

clue.text: Directions to a novice swimmer

parts.note: S and E are the compass directions south and east
L is a learner, from the L-plate

explanation.surface: Instructions given to a beginner learning to swim.
explanation.definitionFit: A seal is a marine mammal, an expert swimmer.

clue.text: First of all, therefore, a goddess

indicators.note: first of means the opening letter of all is taken

parts.note: then can mean therefore, as in 'then it must be true'

explanation.surface: Above all, therefore, a goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints the count as (7), a misprint for 6.
explanation.definitionFit: Athena was the Greek goddess of wisdom and war.

clue.text: Merits A1 treatment taken point by point

indicators.note: treatment means the letters are worked over into a new order

parts.note: A1 is read as the letters A and I

explanation.surface: Merits receiving first-class handling, dealt with item by item.
explanation.walkthrough: The digit 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Seriatim is Latin for one after another in series, item after item.

clue.text: Mineral kept in metal container

indicators.note: kept in signals letters are held inside the words metal container

explanation.surface: A mineral stored in a metal tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Talc is a soft mineral, magnesium silicate, ground into powder.

clue.text: In Europe area of forest and three quarters plateau

definitions.text: In Europe area of forest and three quarters plateau

parts.note: the Forest of Arden is the woodland of As You Like It
the compass quarters north, east and south give N, E and S

explanation.surface: A European region of woodland, three quarters of it upland.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the region: a forested European upland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ardennes is a wooded, hilly plateau region spanning Belgium, Luxembourg and France.

clue.text: A fine sight the tour de France, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is spoken and its sound gives the answer

parts.note: tour is French for tower, and the tower of France is the Eiffel

explanation.surface: A spectator calls the cycle race a lovely sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tour de France' suggests the cycle race, but 'tour' is French for tower.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyeful is something striking to look at, a gratifying view.

clue.text: Guards the ice-bound Styx perhaps?

parts.note: something ice-bound is frozen, cold
the Styx is a river of the underworld, an example of a stream

explanation.surface: Asking whether guards watch over a frozen underworld river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Coldstream Guards are a regiment of the British Army's Household Division.
explanation.definitionFit: The Coldstream Guards are a regiment of the British Army's foot guards.
